# Bridge integration handoff

This package is for integrating **StemWise or Studywell** with the owner's existing bridge. Each app embeds the same SDK and owns its own enrollment, settings, prompts, jobs and imported files. The Raspberry Pi hosts the backend; the Windows PC executes authorized Codex CLI jobs. No additional backend belongs in the app.

Start with `ANDROID.md`, then read `documentation.md` for the complete HTTP contract, report schema, diagnostics, retention and recovery rules. `android/BridgeUsage.java` contains compile-checked call-site examples. `android/API.txt` lists the public methods in the exact packaged AAR. `contracts/app-errors.json` and `contracts/developer-workflow.md` are generated from the current backend and mandatory agent workflow. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers every delivered file. `SOURCE_BUILD.md` explains the included self-contained source/test tree, pinned Windows build and explicit AAR promotion. `android/phone-pc-bridge.build.json` records the delivered AAR and source identities.

The first JSON or file request waits for the exact paired peer's local readiness for up to ten seconds within its operation deadline; startup does not need an arbitrary warm-up delay. Readiness failures expose a structured `bridgeTransportError:"v1"` exception with `phase:"pre_send"` and `requestSent:false` for that exchange. `ANDROID.md` explains cancellation and safe handling; `BridgeUsage.preSendTransportFailure` is a parser, not a retry loop. After an HTTP attempt starts, no automatic mutation replay occurs. These source/build checks do not establish live Android-device acceptance.

For StemWise's unmetered-Wi-Fi-only policy, acquire every shared client using `BridgeRecovery.client(context, "stemwise-bridge", true)`. Factory construction and retained local file recovery remain network-idle. The process-owned policy binds all underlying sockets and DNS to the approved Android Network, suspends the entire node on policy loss/replacement and preserves enrollment, local cache deadlines and accepted Pi work. Restoration permits later SDK calls without resending a job. The two-argument factory retains its active-network policy; it cannot be mixed with the Wi-Fi-only factory in one process.

An accepted/acceptance-unknown request must never be replayed because its GET returned 404. Resolve its original ID with the empty-body `/v2/jobs/<id>/retire` POST: preserve any 200 retained job/result, or persist the authoritative 410 `request_deleted` before enabling local Forget. Retirement means tracking/admission closed with historical execution unknown; it does not prove native execution stopped. Its ID-only barrier expires after 72 hours, so the app's durable no-resubmission rule remains required after cleanup. Local imports and ZIP/import journals stay app-owned. See `ANDROID.md` and `documentation.md` for cancellation, deletion and reconnect behavior.

`DEPLOYMENT.md` provides the compatible Pi/PC host build and maintenance commands for the Bridge maintainer. Android app integration never updates or resets installed hosts automatically. This bundle's source/build verification does not imply that an installed service already contains the changes.

Before app compilation, verify the consumed AAR/manifest pair: `python source/bridge-core/sdk_artifact.py verify --go <pinned-go-executable> --artifact-dir android`. Schema v4 binds the selected Android inputs and candidate source/embed inventory. Unchanged verification uses Python only; candidate changes trigger exact pinned-Go discovery, and `--discover` explicitly requests it. Gradle must track candidate scoped directories as well as selected inputs so added files invalidate its check. Backend/PC-only edits leave the Android identity valid. Full source ships with separate checksums. Android build tools are unnecessary for verification; see `SOURCE_BUILD.md` for the API and input rules.

## Included runtime

- `android/phone-pc-bridge.aar`: embedded userspace transport and Android lifecycle helpers, including dependency licenses. Android 13/API 33 or newer, **arm64-v8a only**, Java 17 integration. Native code uses 16 KiB page alignment.
- The AAR is the dependency to add to your app. Do not install a separate Tailscale app or the bridge's temporary test APK. No APK, enrollment keys, private node state, PC producer credentials or signing keys are included.
- The Pi and PC are already installed. Preserve their configuration. Each app installation must enroll its own embedded node normally in the same owner account; first enrollment/account device approval may require the owner's authorization. Never ship a pre-enrolled directory or embed an account secret. The app owns background scheduling under Android's normal platform and first-unlock rules; the SDK owns the shared embedded client and network callbacks.

## Integration responsibilities

1. Add the AAR, initialize one embedded client per app process, and keep its state in app-private no-backup storage. Reuse that identity across app updates.
2. Implement a **Connection** tab and the app's own **Apps/jobs/prompts/files** controls inside the existing app. Show fresh connection observations, original inputs, outputs and job diagnostics. The app may display its job's developer chat name/ID; never expose conversations, tools or approvals. The installation can manage only its own bridge registration.
3. Register this installation with the actual app name before reading live models, reasoning efforts and service tiers from the API. Each new job receives a fresh bridge-owned native chat automatically after validation; no existing developer-chat binding or conversation selector is required.
4. Own persistent drafts and explicit approval in the app. StemWise requires approval per song before any input upload or job submission. Persist immutable job IDs, original timestamps, reviewed model/effort/serviceTier and optional nativeDefaultServiceTier policy, prompt/custom instructions and file descriptors **before submission**. Keep original user text unchanged. The bridge references its required workflow from its generated Markdown file; do not add it into, replace or paraphrase the user's text.
5. Use file-based streaming for archives. Import and verify every published output into app storage, then acknowledge the exact batch with `Client.confirmDelivery`. Saved app-owned copies survive bridge cleanup. Do not acknowledge delivery before the app actually has the files.
6. Keep transport state, developer task status, verified outputs and independent job error logs separate. A completed native turn, packet receipt or retryable error is not proof of task success. Read the original job after an uncertain submission; never create a replacement automatically.
7. An explicit user Wake, Send to Bridge, Retry or settings Wake action may authorize one empty wake request when needed, separately from job submission. Durably claim at most one attempt for that action before sending. Passive polling, reconnect, startup, job execution, agents, background recovery and automatic retries never authorize wake. Never queue or replay a claimed wake attempt after timeout or restart; another attempt requires a new explicit user action. Preserve the original job IDs and immutable envelope.

For each fresh owned chat, the bridge sends exactly one type=text native user input containing bridgeJobInput:v1 JSON. prompt and customInstructions preserve the originals verbatim, including links; handoffPath, handoffSha256, handoffHeader and readBeforeWork instruct the agent to read and hash-verify the entire real local Markdown handoff before any task work. That file contains the full workflow, current job IDs, file descriptors and runtime paths. The Markdown is not inlined, no extra text/mention inputs are sent, and thread/start carries no Bridge workflow or native developerInstructions. Apps keep their existing HTTP envelope and immutable hashes; the bridge constructs the message. Agents still return strict machine reports; app-readable content belongs in result/output files. There is no bridge-developer chat/contact button. Developer contact initiated inside an app is implemented as that app's ordinary API job, subject to the same workflow and reporting rules.

Model, intelligence and speed controls use `model`, `effort` and optional `serviceTier`. Populate them from the selected live model row's `supportedReasoningEfforts` and `serviceTiers:[{id,name,description}]`; never invent option IDs. A null tier list is unknown; `[]` confirms no explicit choices. `defaultServiceTier:null` does not establish Standard. Explicit `"default"` is usable only if advertised. Missing/empty/null job fields inherit the app's saved values at first admission, then native defaults; later settings changes do not rewrite accepted work. Send explicit choices to bind a reviewed selection. Settings PUT replaces all saved choices, with missing/empty/null clearing a saved value. An explicit resolved tier without a resolved model returns HTTP 400 `service_tier_model_required`; confirmed unsupported tiers use `service_tier_unavailable`, while unconfirmed catalog capability remains retryable `model_catalog_unavailable`. Captured choices appear in the job view and are forwarded unchanged, but do not prove effective native speed or account entitlement. See `documentation.md` for exact validation and conflict behavior.

To use native tier policy for one job even when the app saved a priority tier, include `"nativeDefaultServiceTier":true` in its immutable POST `/v2/jobs` envelope and leave `serviceTier` absent, empty or null. The captured tier is empty and the PC sends no tier override; this does not establish Standard or Fast. For example, `{"model":"gpt-6-luna","effort":"max","nativeDefaultServiceTier":true}` requests that behavior when the model/effort are supported. True with a nonempty tier returns HTTP 400 `invalid_service_tier_choice`. Omitted/false/null preserves existing inheritance and hashes of requests without this flag; model/effort behavior is unchanged. Persist the flag with the reviewed draft and original request; changing it on an accepted ID conflicts. It belongs to the immutable job input, not settings PUT.

For recoverable input uploads use `FileClient.ensureSent` with the persisted original transfer ID and a fresh reserved SDK phase. It probes the exact receipt and sends only after authenticated absence; an uncertain or corrupt receipt is an explicit failure. Cheap metadata and bounded storage diagnostics do not establish payload validity. Actual use and whole-batch publication retain byte verification. Native waits release the app-state lock and recheck the saved job/registration before applying results. Proven no-send creation and explicit native rejection release only their exact unchanged reservation and produce distinct diagnostic codes. Recovery still observes that original reservation and repeats the unchanged create only after authenticated absence; a reserved uncertain creation is never replayed. A created but never-dispatched chat owns no file references, so it cannot pin unrelated caches. Current dispatch/input and output ownership records preserve interrupted commits without historical index reconstruction. Cleanup diagnostics expose unresolved handoff count/age while keeping other apps' owner IDs private.

Windows managed-file publication tolerates temporary directory access/sharing denials with a cancellable retry window of one second. Only the final rename of the same complete staged object is retried; source reads, uploads and jobs are not replayed. Permanent or unrelated filesystem failures remain explicit. Other platforms retain a single publication rename.

One coordinator discovers actual pending work before one PC health probe and shares it with four fixed job workers; healthy idle apps cause no repeated automatic probes. Job/cancellation/delivery changes coalesce into a wakeup, and pending work or discovery failure keeps ten-second reconnect polling. At most two job turns per app run concurrently. Every request owns a fresh chat; fair selection and exact job leases keep a held transfer/history lookup from locking the whole app. Durable cancellation stops that job's current IO context; retirement releases its slot, and explicit owner removal also closes an owned output body. Native select/send remains globally serialized, with cancellable waiting and a current-state reload. Observation passes handle up to eight jobs with a rotating cursor. These are scheduling bounds, not measured throughput or latency guarantees; network/body cancellation and local filesystem calls require cooperative return. A cancelled or removed job is never dispatched from an old snapshot; this scheduler never requests wake.

## Deterministic boundaries and different app workflows

The bridge enforces its transport and report protocol in ordinary code. Mandatory prompting explains the contract to an agent; prompting is not the validator. The bridge cannot guarantee identical LLM answers, fixed execution time, complete diagnosis of every underlying failure or the semantic correctness of a generated file.

| Layer | Authoritative source and checks |
|---|---|
| Bridge connection/job state | Authenticated reachability, durable reservations, exact native acknowledgment/history and validated state transitions. Missing evidence remains unknown/unconfirmed. Connection observations expire. |
| Bridge/API errors | Fixed machine codes and structured message/retryable/action fields. Native/bridge diagnostics are recorded independently of developer task status. |
| Developer task report | Exact app/job IDs, strict field/type/status validation, committed native message/turn evidence and monotonically increasing revisions. The reported task status/cause remains the developer's claim. |
| Files and delivery | Actual file ownership, size and SHA-256 checks, whole-batch publication, verified imported destination bytes and explicit app acknowledgment. Byte integrity does not prove that the file satisfies an app's business schema. |
| App-specific meaning | The integrating app's ordinary code validates its own result schema, known domain codes, expected files and application rules before using the data. |

StemWise and Studywell use the same outer API and report schema, but have separate authenticated registrations, prompts/settings, jobs, diagnostics and files. Developer report `status` is always one of `working`, `waiting`, `completed`, `failed`; use `code` for app-specific stages or reasons. For example, `stemwise_validating_input` and `studywell_processing_items` are illustrative custom codes, not new universal status values. Bridge/native job `state`, `report.status`, `report.code`, independent `/log`, verified `outputs`, `delivered` and `chatState` must remain separate in the app's UI/state logic.

For each app, define a versioned machine contract: supported stages/error codes, input/output JSON schemas, required file roles, deterministic validation rules and the meaning of successful import. Supply that context in the job's instructions HTTP field and/or declared input context file. The bridge preserves those instructions and the original prompt in distinct JSON fields within its single native message; its common workflow stays in the referenced Markdown file. Saved prompts are stored templates: the app selects and snapshots the intended text/instructions into each immutable submitted job. Existing queued jobs are not rewritten by later prompt/settings changes.

The current bridge validates the syntax of custom developer codes, not a registered per-app code allowlist. It transfers opaque file bytes and has no per-app schema-registry or semantic-validator endpoint. Therefore code/schema acceptance must be implemented in each app's deterministic import logic; instructions alone do not enforce that vocabulary. Unknown domain codes must remain visibly unrecognized, not silently mapped to success. Keep app-specific structured payloads in declared JSON output files; arbitrary extra fields in the outer job/report envelope are rejected. All agent failed reports require a structured diagnostic, but a missing/malformed report produces a bridge protocol diagnostic rather than an invented original cause.

An integration may require a stricter application-success condition than bridge delivery. For example, after a valid ZIP is imported, the app may reject its internal JSON schema while transport and checksum verification have succeeded. Preserve those two outcomes separately. The app can acknowledge verified byte delivery once the complete batch is safely saved and verified; that acknowledgment is not a claim that downstream parsing or business processing succeeded.

## App-owned typed dispatcher

StemWise can submit one immutable bridge job per song; each receives a fresh bridge-owned Codex chat. The app can supply separate custom instructions naming a fixed, app-owned dispatcher command and attach a versioned JSON context file as a declared input. The dispatcher owns schema validation, permitted operations, song identity, processing and result validation. Treat context values as data, never executable shell text or permission grants. The bridge job API has no command/project selector or generic process-execution endpoint: Codex invokes the dispatcher through its ordinary permitted native tools, in the host's configured project context.

Use the authenticated producer executable, private state and exact paired peer from the injected handoff. For every declared input ID, call `-files-op received-info -id <id>`, compare the returned `file` descriptor to the immutable job descriptor, then call `-files-op read -id <id> -file <new absolute project destination>`. Check command success and the returned descriptor; `read` verifies actual bytes before preserving that new destination. Invoke the fixed dispatcher with those project-owned inputs. Queue actual output files with `-files-op queue -app-id <exact handoff app ID> -job-id <exact handoff job ID> -thread-id <exact handoff thread ID> -id <stable output ID> -file <absolute source>`; obtain each fresh output ID by parsing the `.id` of `-files-op new-id` JSON, persist it before queueing and copy the queue reply's exact `file` descriptor unchanged into the final report. Never write directly to managed stores or publish local paths as outputs.

Return only strict `bridgeJobReport:v2` messages for the exact app/job IDs, with increasing revisions and a terminal `completed` or `failed` report. A completed claim requires actual dispatcher results and queued descriptors; the bridge additionally requires committed native report/turn evidence and verifies the whole output batch. The app must still validate its versioned result schema before applying it. Native execution permissions remain authoritative: unavailable capability produces a structured failure, not an approval bypass. After uncertain dispatch, observe the original job; neither another chat nor a replacement job may replay unverified side effects. The dispatcher must separately make any retryable app-side operation safe under its own durable operation identity.

## Acceptance in each app

Complete enrollment once, preserve it through updates, and check independent connection/authentication freshness. Confirm unapproved drafts send no inputs or jobs. Only when authorized, submit one owned fixture job and verify immutable choices, real input/output bytes, independent logs, delivery and native cleanup. Use isolated executable fixtures to test account changes while idle/active, provider preflight failure, unchanged accepted IDs, restart and final source/event fences. Test every job state at created+72h, expiry during transfers, output claims persisted before bytes, offline PC cleanup delegation, restart recovery, shared-owner protection and bounded cleanup capacity. Explicit deletion and expired-job cleanup must not replay work or remove app-owned imports/settings/prompts. Observe codexAuth, expiredJobCleanup, chatCleanup and backgroundOperations independently. Do not submit a real app job or change devices/accounts as an integration probe without owner approval.

See the final verification section in `documentation.md` for the exact tested conditions and remaining operational limits. Readiness for integration does not promise availability during power loss, expired account enrollment or unavailable native execution capability.

Local cancellation is scoped to each complete synchronous SDK call, including its internal network stages and local copying/hashing. Local file operations take a caller-owned operation ID first; see SOURCE_BUILD.md and android/API.txt. App-owned workflow cancellation must remain latched across separate SDK calls, and a cancelled HTTP mutation still needs receipt reconciliation. Server job cancellation uses the existing cancel endpoint and remains pending through uncertain dispatch, interruption and exact owned execution retirement. The source build promotes a checked AAR/manifest pair only when `-PublishTo` explicitly names the consumed dependency directory; run the cheap identity check from SOURCE_BUILD.md before app compilation.

For cancellable scheduled work, reserve client.newOperation() before worker publication and pass its one-use token to the SDK call. This closes the cancel-before-registration race. SOURCE_BUILD.md gives the supported parent-lock/FutureTask handoff, abandonment cleanup and actual retirement rules. Each separate SDK call gets a fresh lease; original server job/transfer IDs stay unchanged.
